It's as simple as that: keep your surfaces clean, that is, don't put things on them unless they are being used. There are few things more beautiful than a free-flowing, open, flat surface, be it a desk, a dining table, a nightstand, &c.

When we see these empty spaces we feel compelled to fill them. Maybe this is from years of 'fill-in-the-blank' schooling. But not only is there no real reason to fill up / use this empty space, in fact, there's a very convincing reason why we SHOULDN'T! These spaces are only useful when they are clear. Suddenly have to do a lot of paperwork? Just bust out whatever you need to work on, right now - your desk is clear, right? Have an unexpected guest over? Good thing the dining table is cleared off - and if you needed to whip something together, then it's a good thing the kitchen counters are open, too... right?

This should be a high-priority exercise. Clear surfaces. You are not being 'inefficient' by letting the space 'just sit there'. You need to be able to escape this sort of thinking - and it is very hard to do in some societies / cultures. You are not an 'incomplete' person because you have an empty shelf in your apartment. In fact, if you want extra credit you should try to find ways to get rid of the shelf! We give meaning to the things we own, not the other way around. But exploring this mindset further is for another day. For now, fight the battle: keep your surfaces open, clean, and uncluttered. And of course this applies to the largest surface in your dwelling: the floor!
